submission.justification: Selection-S3 (gradient-boosted classifier) gave the highest expected significance at every working point tested, with a peak around 40-50% signal efficiency: 4.07 sigma at 40%, 4.02 at 50%, 3.89 at 60%, 3.85 at 70%, 3.76 at 30%. Selection-S2 peaked at about 3.34 sigma and Selection-S1 at about 2.58 sigma. The 2025 summary (4.1/3.4/2.6 sigma at 50%) is consistent with these results. I chose 40% because it has the highest value in the scan, though the difference from 50% is small. The sensitivity tool reports statistical uncertainty only. No document quantifies background systematics, so the robustness of the background estimate is not verified. This is a concern for S3 specifically, since it uses jet substructure variables that may be harder to model than the kinematic-only S2. Before unblinding, the background estimate for S3 should be checked for systematic robustness (for example, data-driven control regions or comparison with S2 as a cross-check).
